title: QUIC RFC 9000 S17P2P4 Handshake Packet Format Proof Tail
purpose: Describe the focused S17P2P4 closure for handshake packet header parsing, packet-number zero send semantics, coalesced receive handling, and allowed-versus-forbidden handshake payload proofs.
design_summary: Handshake packets remain long-header version 1 packets parsed through the shared packet parser and formatted through the coordinator with the fixed four-byte packet-number field. The focused proof covers connection-ID parsing, the first server handshake packet number zero boundary, client receipt of Initial-only versus coalesced Initial+Handshake flights, and allowed versus forbidden handshake frame payloads.
data_and_state_considerations: The proof stays in requirement-home tests and canonical trace metadata. Packet-number state is exercised through the existing coordinator reflection helper, while client and server TLS state observations stay limited to handshake-key and transport-parameter commit boundaries exposed by the test support. The slice does not widen public APIs or add new packet-format surfaces.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Initial-only server receipt does not yet commit peer transport parameters.
Coalesced Initial+Handshake receipt does commit peer transport parameters.
A truncated protected handshake packet cannot be opened.
The handshake packet-number counter reaches the uint.MaxValue boundary without losing the four-byte encoding.
Handshake packets carrying CRYPTO, PING, PADDING, ACK, or CONNECTION_CLOSE remain allowed, while RESET_STREAM remains forbidden.
risks: This slice does not alter runtime packet handling.
This slice does not widen public packet APIs.
This slice does not claim hosted interop readiness.
This slice does not close unrelated deferred fuzz obligations.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the focused S17P2P4 hard proof tail for REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S17P2P4-0003, REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S17P2P4-0016, REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S17P2P4-0017, REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S17P2P4-0018, REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S17P2P4-0019, REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S17P2P4-0020, and REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S17P2P4-0021. It does not claim broader RFC 9000 packet-family closure, public API widening, hosted interop readiness, or closure of unrelated deferred fuzz obligations.
